chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام was asked about a well into which a basket of dry or wet feces falls, and he said: “There is no harm in it if there is much water in it.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His statement, “There is no harm in it,” means when fifty buckets have been drawn from it, according to what we have previously explained regarding it.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.خَمْسُونَ دَلْوًا: fifty buckets, the number specified in the explanatory ruling
key_terms.رَطْبَةٍ: wet, describing another possible state of the filth
key_terms.زِنْبِيلُ: a basket or container that fell into the well
key_terms.عَذِرَةٍ: feces or filth causing concern of contamination
key_terms.مَاءٌ كَثِيرٌ: abundant water, indicating a quantity relevant to the ruling
key_terms.نُزِحَ: water was drawn out, referring to the prescribed removal
key_terms.يَابِسَةٍ: dry, describing one possible state of the filth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a well if a basket of feces falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a well into which a basket of filth falls. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm if the well contains abundant water, and Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains this as applying after drawing fifty buckets from it. The report is significant in discussions of taharah and the legal rulings of water.
